analysis.title: Commodity Call: Aluminium market tightness easing
key_insights: Aluminium has been among the commodities most affected by the Middle East conflict, which accounts for 8% of global production. Regional losses kept the market tight in H1 2026.
Recovering Middle East output, resilient Chinese production and strong Indonesian supply growth should narrow this year's deficit and move the market into surplus in 2027.

Middle East production has recovered faster than expected. Al Taweelah in the UAE has restarted 50% of capacity, and more than 90% of affected production (1,555kt) is likely to resume in 2027. Annual losses should be under 2mt versus earlier estimates of 3-3.5mt.
China's smelters are running above the 45mt capacity cap because of strong margins, but the cap has 300-500kt of leeway. ANZ expects China to produce 45.4mt in 2027, a material slowdown in growth.
Indonesian output is forecast to rise from 709kt in 2026 to 1.3mt in 2027 and 2.9mt by 2030. It has already offset half of this year's Middle East losses.
Global aluminium output is estimated flat in 2026 and should grow by more than 4% to 77.8mt in 2027, against demand growth of 2.5-2.7% to 77.5mt.
Surplus in 2027 should cap price upside, but lingering Middle East supply risks should keep prices volatile and above USD3,000/t through early 2027.

Oil: ANZ raised its 31 Dec Brent forecast from USD95/bbl to USD105/bbl. Hormuz throughput is about 60% of normal, distillate inventories are below the five-year average and effective OPEC spare capacity is negligible.
LNG: Persian Gulf supply losses could reach 55mt in 2026. European storage reached 75% by 1 November against an 80% target, and prices are expected to stay elevated through winter.
Copper: prices retreated on macro pressure, with downside protected near USD13,500/t because concentrate tightness is unlikely to ease. Chilean output is down 7% to 3.2mt so far this year.
Nickel: LME inventories are near 275kt versus under 100kt in 2024. Upside is limited, with support near USD15,000/t.
Gold: ANZ expects a USD3,800-4,000/oz range in coming weeks. It expects the Fed to resume rate hikes in December. ETF holdings fell by 20t while central-bank demand stays resilient.
Silver: prices should stabilise around USD50/oz. Silver demand is forecast to contract 2% to 1,113moz in 2026 as solar manufacturers reduce silver intensity.
Iron ore: ANZ is cautious near term. China's September steel output was 73.6mt, down 6mt y/y, and port stocks are near 165mt, up 13% y/y.
EUAs are expected in the mid-to-high EUR80/t near term and EUR85-90/t through 2027. ACCUs are expected around the high-AUD30s to low-AUD40s/t through 2027.
El Niño is strengthening, with NOAA giving a probability above 83% of a strong-to-very-strong event through January-March 2027.

sector_views.rationale: Market shifts to surplus in 2027 as Middle East, Indonesian and Chinese supply outpaces demand growth, capping upside.
Brent forecast raised to USD105/bbl on depleted buffers and constrained Gulf exports, with risks skewed to the upside.
Weak Chinese steel demand, high port stocks and rising supply from Simandou, Australia and Brazil.
Tighter monetary policy offsets resilient central bank and physical demand, giving a USD3,800-4,000/oz range.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Persistent physical tightness leaves risks skewed to the upside.
Renewed Middle East attacks pushed prices to a monthly high.

macro_indicators.reading: Rate hike expected in December after hold in October
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher energy prices and strong growth support ANZ's call for renewed tightening, a headwind for gold.
Fed held rates, but oil-driven inflation risk weighed on sentiment.
Supply growth outpaces demand and flips the market into surplus.
Central bank buying offsets tighter policy.
Short of the 80% target, leaving Europe exposed to cold weather or supply disruptions.
Down 6mt y/y, reflecting weak mill margins and demand.

risk_factors: Lingering Middle East supply risks could keep aluminium prices volatile.
Delays to data-centre projects and AI valuation concerns cloud power-infrastructure and aluminium demand.
A renewed supply shock to oil could have a larger impact because buffers are depleted.
Renewed US strikes on Iran are a key tail risk for LNG.
Cold weather or fresh supply disruptions could hit Europe's lean gas storage.
A restoration of Russian gas flows is the key downside risk to European gas prices.
Renewed ETF selling could weaken gold's support.
If US copper import tariffs are not imposed, copper could flow out of the US and pressure prices.
vol_and_positioning: ANZ expects aluminium prices to stay volatile and above USD3,000/t through early 2027.
Gold-backed ETF holdings fell by 20t in recent weeks as investors sold gold to raise cash. Further liquidation is flagged as the near-term downside risk.
Copper is increasingly correlated with technology and AI sentiment.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict has cut aluminium, oil and LNG supply. Hormuz throughput is around 60% of normal.
Renewed US attacks on Iran after the US midterm elections are flagged as a near-term catalyst and LNG tail risk.
Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi said the country would continue to give diplomacy a chance, and President Trump said negotiations were taking place through mediators.
Several Persian Gulf nations were notified to prepare for a short, intense military campaign.
QatarEnergy extended force majeure on LNG shipments to Italy and Asian customers.
The US is pushing for a restoration of Russian gas flows to Europe.
Ukrainian forces are targeting Russian refineries, reducing Russian product flows.
US tariff uncertainty on copper imports is keeping the market tight and volatile.

tension_points.bull_case: Lingering Middle East supply risks and structural demand from EVs, solar and power transmission, where aluminium is substituting for copper, keep prices volatile and above USD3,000/t through early 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Faster Middle East restarts, Indonesian growth and supply growth above 4% against demand growth of 2.5-2.7% flip the market into surplus in 2027 and cap upside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed Middle East supply disruption, or data-centre and AI-related demand weakening further, would change the balance.

theme_stances.key_argument: Supply growth should outpace demand as Middle East metal returns and Indonesian projects ramp up, flipping the market into surplus in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: supply growth should outpace demand, flipping the market into surplus in 2027

theme_stances.key_argument: Eight months of disruption have eroded buffers, leaving risks to oil skewed to the upside.
